source_tasks.problem: The expression $4 \times  5 +  2 -  8 -  3 +  3 \times  5$ may be changed only by inserting parentheses; rearranging numbers or operations is not allowed. In total, how many values can be obtained?

Consider the expression $4 +  8 -  6 \cdot  6 -  4 +  2 \cdot  7$. Fully parenthesize it in every possible way without changing the order of numbers or operations. Parenthesizations with the same numerical result count only once. How many distinct values are possible?
The expression $7 +  6 \times  8 -  6 +  5 \times  3 -  5$ may be changed only by inserting parentheses; rearranging numbers or operations is not allowed. In total, how many values can be obtained?

interface_note: Only parameter values vary; all mathematical conditions and requested quantity remain those stated by the supplied source questions. Names describe source data, not a target algorithm. Implement solve(parameters), no natural-language applicability detection. operators must have exactly len(operands)-1 entries.

observations: All three source tasks ask for the number of distinct values obtainable by fully parenthesizing a fixed sequence of operands and binary operators (+,-,*), preserving order.

The mathematical object is the set of results over all binary parenthesizations of an expression with n operands and n-1 operators; this is exactly interval dynamic programming over sets of achievable values.
The number of full parenthesizations is Catalan(n-1), but the requested quantity is the cardinality of the union of resulting values, so duplicates must be merged.
Failures show two recurring errors: (a) enumerating or estimating instead of computing the exact set, and (b) truncation from manual enumeration; both are avoided by a deterministic set-based DP.
The interface fixes operands and operators with len(operators)=len(operands)-1, so the procedure is well-defined for any valid parameter instance.
analysis.procedure_plan: Let operands a[0..n-1] and operators op[0..n-2], where op[k] sits between a[k] and a[k+1]. Define dp[i][j] as the set of all integer values obtainable by fully parenthesizing the subexpression a[i..j]. Base: dp[i][i]={a[i]}. For length L=2..n, for each i with j=i+L-1, initialize dp[i][j]=empty set; for each split k from i to j-1, combine every x in dp[i][k] with every y in dp[k+1][j] using op[k] (+,-,*), inserting x+y, x-y, or x*y into dp[i][j]. Use a set (or hash set) at each interval to deduplicate. Return the cardinality of dp[0][n-1]. Handle n=1 by returning 1 (the single operand). This directly computes the exact number of distinct values; no Catalan enumeration or manual listing is needed.
analysis.uncertainty: The procedure is standard and exact for the stated quantity. Residual uncertainty is only about whether the grader expects the count for the exact given operand/operator sequences (it does per the interface); no semantic ambiguity remains. Complexity is exponential in the worst case because value sets can grow, but for the supplied sizes (n<=8, operands in [-10,20]) it is feasible with set-based DP.
